desc: Precompute two arrays: `prefix_max[i]` storing the maximum subarray sum in `nums[0...i]` and `suffix_max[i]` storing the maximum subarray sum in `nums[i...n-1]`.
Identify the first and last occurrence indices for every unique number present in `nums`.
Iterate through each unique number $x$; for each $x$, calculate the maximum possible subarray sum if $x$ is removed by considering:
The max subarray sum in the range `[0, first_occurrence[x] - 1]`.
The max subarray sum in the range `[last_occurrence[x] + 1, n - 1]`.
The sum of the rightmost part of the prefix (ending at `first_occurrence[x] - 1`) and the leftmost part of the suffix (starting at `last_occurrence[x] + 1`).
Also consider the case where no operation is performed (original array's max subarray sum) and return the global maximum found.
Verify the solution with provided examples (Example 1: `[-3,2,-2,-1,3,-2,3]` -> 7, Example 2: `[1,2,3,4]` -> 10).
Check constraints and potential integer overflow (Python handles large integers automatically).
Ensure the code is self-contained and imports are correct.

Refactor the solution to use the Segment Tree approach as identified in the worker notes, since the current prefix/suffix logic fails to handle the "middle" segment between the first and last occurrence of the removed element $x$.
